fallback.text: The exact coverage of two 95 % intervals for a proportion, with n = 30. The textbook Wald interval p̂ ± 1.96·√(p̂(1−p̂)/n) covers the true p only 80.9 % of the time at p = 0.1 and averages 87.9 % over all p, falling to almost nothing near 0 and 1. The Wilson interval, which inverts the score test, covers 97.4 % at p = 0.1 and averages 95.2 %. The curves are jagged because k can only be a whole number (Brown, Cai and DasGupta, 2001).
